hindi: छह अंगुल ऊँचा और बत्तीस घेरे वाला: शिर।
english: Six finger-breadths (aṅgula) in height and thirty-two in girth: the head.

text_flags.why: possible: printed as one word with the hiatus closed up; regular sandhi of śiraḥ + iti is 'śira iti' (spacing error)

notes: Elliptical: no verb is stated, none is supplied. GROUPING: appears to continue from the previous unit (the subject of the measures is the head, śiras, named at the end). The closing 'iti' marks the end of the statement and is not translated. Orthography: anusvāra for a class nasal (ṣaḍaṃgula = ṣaḍaṅgula, daṃta = danta) is the print's habit and is normalised in `w` without a flag in this chunk; doubled rtt/rdd (varttā, varddhamāna) likewise normalised to rt/rd. aṅgula = finger-breadth, a unit of body measure.

hindi: फिर सारा शरीर चौरासी अंगुल है।
english: Again, the whole body is eighty-four finger-breadths (aṅgula).
notes: Copula understood (none stated). The plural aṅgulāni and singular caturaśītiḥ do not agree in number; the sense is a measure equation. The count (84) is translated as printed.

hindi: उस लम्बाई और चौड़ाई में बराबर को सम यानी बराबर कहा जाता है।
english: What is equal in that length and breadth is called sama (even, symmetrical).
notes: tad is read as 'that (length and breadth)', i.e. the measure just given. The unstated noun (the body) is not supplied. 'sama' is given as 'even, symmetrical'; the text does not say more. Reviewer: alternative parse tad (separate pronoun, nom. n. sg.) + āyāma-vistāra-samam, i.e. 'that, equal in length and breadth, is called sama'; tadā ('then') is also possible. Open for the owner.

hindi: उनमें कहा गया परिमाण इष्ट है; कम या अधिक अनिष्ट है।
english: Therein, the measure as stated is desirable (iṣṭa); deficient or excessive is undesirable (aniṣṭa).
notes: Copula understood. The division of the clauses (iṣṭam | aniṣṭam hīnam adhikam vā) is the natural reading; hīnam/adhikam could also be read directly with the measure.

hindi: इस प्रकार, निश्चय ही:
english: Thus indeed:
notes: Formula 'tathā hi' introducing what follows (examples or a list); it is not said what follows.

words.gloss: short; tall (long); fair; dark; hairy (roma); hairless (aroma); stout; lean

hindi: ह्रस्व यानी छोटा, दीर्घ यानी लम्बा, गोरा, काला, रोम वाला, रोम रहित, स्थूल यानी मोटा और कृश यानी दुबला।
english: Short, tall, fair, dark, hairy, hairless, stout and lean.
notes: One neuter dvandva of eight qualities. The closing 'iti' is not translated. The unit appears to follow 'tathā hi' (u116) and to give instances of body forms; the text does not say so.

hindi: इष्ट, फिर, बड़े सिर, दाँत, मुख, हनु यानी जबड़े, स्तनाग्र, पीठ और स्वर वाला; पुष्ट ऊरु यानी जाँघ, नितम्ब, कमर, छाती, गरदन और तालु वाला; दोनों गुणों वाले हाथ, पैर, ठोड़ी, कान और माथे वाला; सूक्ष्म हड्डी, दाँत, नाखून, उँगलियों के पर्व यानी जोड़ और केश वाला; लम्बी उँगलियों, सक्थि यानी जाँघ, भुजा, अनुमानित पाठ पर श्वास, दृष्टि, नेत्र और जीभ वाला; चौड़े मुख, निचले होंठ, जीभ, माथे, कर्णपीठ और छाती वाला, तथा छोटे मेढ्र यानी शिश्न, गरदन और केश वाला; चिकना, अस्पष्ट छपा त्वकचकरजन, नेत्र, दाँत और स्वर वाला; स्थिर इन्द्रिय, त्वचा, नाखून, केश और पार्श्व यानी पसलियों वाले भाग वाला; गहरी नाभि, जोड़ और स्वर वाला; छिपे हुए जत्रु यानी सम्भवतः हँसली का स्थान, पृष्ठवंश यानी रीढ़ और दाँतों की जड़ वाला; लाल तालु, होंठ, नाखून और नेत्रों के कोनों वाला तथा हल्के लाल जीभ, हाथ और पैर के तलों वाला; काले केश, भौंह, नेत्र, पलकों और तारक यानी पुतली वाला, अस्पष्ट छपा शुक्लशुकमण्डलदशनचरित वाला, ऊँचे, छपे अनुसार चित्त, कन्धे, माथे, पेट, मुख, नाखून और पैर वाला; नीचे बँधे कान, स्तन, नासाग्र और चाल वाला; घने कन्धे और गरदन वाला, अस्पष्ट छपा वंतांगुलि वाला, त्वचा और सुहृद् भाव वाला।
english: Desirable, moreover, (is one) with: large head, teeth, face, jaws (hanu), breast-tips, back and voice; well-developed thighs, buttocks, waist, chest, neck and palate; hands, feet, chin, ears and forehead having both qualities; fine bones, teeth, nails, finger-joints and hair; long fingers, thighs (sakthi), arms, breath (on a conjectural reading), gaze, eyes and tongue; broad mouth, lower lip, tongue, forehead, ear-seat and chest, and small penis (meḍhra), neck and hair; smooth, (unclear: the printed 'tvakacakarajana'), eyes, teeth and voice; steady sense-organs (indriya), skin, nails, hair and sides; deep navel, joints and voice; hidden jatru (probably the collarbone region), spine (pṛṣṭhavaṃśa) and tooth-roots; red palate, lips, nails and eye-corners, and reddish tongue, palms and soles; black hair, eyebrows, eyes, eyelashes and pupil; (unclear: the printed 'śuklaśukaṃmaṃḍaladaśanacaritam'); raised mind (citta, as printed), shoulders, forehead, belly, face, nails and feet; low-set ears, breasts, nose-tip and gait; dense shoulders and neck; (unclear: the printed 'vaṃtāṃguli'); skin and friendliness (sauhārda).

text_flags.why: possible: 'ccch' has an extra c and 'ucchāsa' is not a word; ucchvāsa (breath) fits; the whole member is doubtful, so the translation marks it 'on a conjectural reading'
possible: 'lālaṭā' is not a word, lalāṭa (forehead) is used elsewhere in this unit; 'meṃḍhra' read as the usual meḍhra (penis), a spelling variant of the anusvāra-for-ḍ type
possible: 'jivhā' is a variant spelling of jihvā (tongue); normalised in `words`
possible damage: 'tvakacakarajana' cannot be divided with confidence (tvak + kaca? + kara? + jana(na)?); kept unsplit and marked unclear

possible damage: 'śuklaśukaṃmaṃḍaladaśanacarita' has no sure reading (śukla, maṇḍala and daśana are recognisable but 'śuka' and 'carita' do not fit); kept unsplit and marked unclear; 'citta' (mind) among body parts is also doubtful
possible damage: 'vaṃtāṃguli' after kandharā has no sure reading; kept unsplit and marked unclear

notes: A very long run of bahuvrīhi adjectives (all nom./acc. sg.), joined in the print without spaces, in the style of a description of a desirable body. No noun is stated in this unit; the later units (to u136, where 'śarīram' stands) appear to continue the same description. GROUPING: appears to continue into u119 (same construction). Scope doubts: whether mahā 'large' applies to every member of its compound (head ... voice), whether upacita applies to all of 'thigh ... palate', whether dīrgha applies to every member of its compound, and what 'both qualities' (ubhaya-guṇa) refers to, are not settled by the Sanskrit; translated in the most literal way. 'stanāgra' = breast-tip (probable: nipple). 'karṇa-pīṭha' is literally ear-seat; the exact part is unclear. 'jatru' = collarbone region (probable). 'pṛṣṭha-vaṃśa' = spine (probable). 'meḍhra' = penis (standard). 'adhara-oṣṭha' taken as one item 'lower lip'; it could be two items (lower lip, lip). 'ātāmra' = reddish. 'netrānta' = corners/ends of the eyes. 'caṅkramaṇa' = walking, gait; 'nīcair baddha' = set low. 'citta' is printed 'mind' among body parts and is probably a misprint (not corrected). 'sauhārda' = friendliness, goodwill. Printed 'ucchāsa' conjecturally read as ucchvāsa (breath). Three stretches are unreadable and kept unsplit (tvakacakarajana; śuklaśukaṃmaṃḍaladaśanacarita; vaṃtāṃguli); translations leave them 'unclear' and give no meaning. Low confidence throughout. Reviewer conjecture, not applied: 'tvakacakarajana' + 'nayana' may be tvak-kaca-karaja-(na)-nayana, i.e. skin, hair, nails (karaja), eyes, within the snigdha series; one stray 'na'. For śuklaśukaṃmaṃḍaladaśanacarita a śukla-śaṅkha-… reading is conceivable; no sure reading.
lines_deva: इष्टं च पुनर्महाशिरोदशनवदनहनुस्तनाग्रपृष्ठस्वरमुपचितोरुस्फिककटिवक्षोग्रीवातालुकमुभयगुणपाणिपादचुबुककर्णललाटं सूक्ष्मास्थिदंतनखांगुलिपर्वकेशं दीर्घांगुलिसक्थिबाहूच्च्छासेक्षितनेत्रजिह्वं विस्तीर्णास्याधरोष्ठजिह्वलालटाकर्णपीठवक्षोऽल्पमेंढ्रग्रीवाकेशं स्निग्धत्वकचकरजननयनदशनस्वनं स्थिरेंद्रियत्वङ्नखकेशपार्श्वं गंभीरनाभिसंधिस्वरं गूढजत्रुपृष्ठवंशदंतमूलं रक्तताल्वोष्ठनखनेत्रांतमाताम्रजिव्हाहस्तपादतलं कृष्णकेशभ्रूनेत्रपक्ष्मतारकंशुक्लशुकंमंडलदशनचरितमुन्नतचित्तस्कंधललाटोदरमुखनखपादं नीचैर्बद्धकर्णस्तननासाग्रचंक्रमणं घनस्कंधकंधरावंतांगुलित्वक्सौहार्दं

words.gloss: even; back; tooth; forehead; look, gaze

hindi: हनु यानी जबड़ा, अस्पष्ट छपा नवमद्य और जीभ वाला; गोल नितम्ब, गरदन और नाखून वाला; समतल पीठ, दाँत, माथे और दृष्टि वाला।
english: (One) with jaw (hanu), (unclear: the printed 'navamadya') and tongue; round buttocks, neck and nails; even back, teeth, forehead and gaze.

text_flags.why: possible damage: 'navamadya' has no sure reading ('madya' may be a misprint of madhya, 'middle'); kept unsplit and marked unclear

notes: Continues the series of adjectives of u118 (GROUPING: appears to continue u118). hanu, 'jaw'. 'navamadya' cannot be read with confidence (nava 'new/nine', madya 'intoxicating drink' make no sense among body parts; madhya 'middle' is possible); no meaning is given. jihvam is taken as the last member of a compound with hanu and the unclear piece, which is itself uncertain. 'īkṣita' = look, gaze. Low confidence.

hindi: तथा क्रम से गोल दोनों जाँघें।
english: Likewise, the two thighs (ūru) rounded in due succession.
notes: The avagraha after -ā (tathā'nupūrva) is a print habit; the sandhi is regular tathā + anupūrva. 'anupūrva-vṛtta' = 'rounded in due order', usually understood as evenly tapering; only the literal sense is given. Elliptical: no verb.

hindi: नाभि दक्षिणावर्त यानी दाहिनी ओर घूमी हुई है।
english: The navel (nābhi) is right-turning (dakṣiṇāvarta).
notes: Copula understood. dakṣiṇāvarta is literally 'turning to the right'; nothing more is said. The doubled tt (dakṣiṇāvarttā) is normalised.

words.gram: m. nom. du.; f. nom. du.

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, बड़े अन्तर वाले दोनों स्तन और दोनों भौंहें।
english: On a conjectural reading, the two breasts and the two eyebrows having a wide interval.

text_flags.why: possible: the ā-sign is missing before the anusvāra (prakṛṣṭā+ntarau); 'prakṛṣṭa-antara' = having a wide interval fits stanau-bhruvau
possible: spacing error; au + bh has no sandhi, so two words (stanau, bhruvau), not a compound

notes: stanau-bhruvau is printed as one word: stanau + bhruvau, regular dual forms. The corrected word prakṛṣṭāntarau is used in `words` and in the translation, which is marked as conjectural; as printed 'prakṛṣṭaṃtarau' it is not a word. The wide interval is taken to hold between the two members of each pair; the text does not state this. Elliptical: no verb.

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, नाखूनों और दोनों पैरों में कछुए जैसी उठान।
english: On a conjectural reading, tortoise-like elevations in the nails and the two feet.

text_flags.why: possible: printed 'ā' for 'o'; kūrma-unnati (tortoise-like elevation) fits nails and feet; the plural nakhāḥ/dual pādau do not agree in number, so the reading is not firm

notes: Reading uncertain: 'kūrmānnatayo' is not a regular word; kūrma-unnati (f.) 'tortoise-like rise' is taken, with -ḥ before nakhāḥ giving -o. Another possibility is kūrma-unnata 'raised like a tortoise' as an adjective (nakhāḥ pādau ca). Elliptical: no verb.

words.gloss: nose; ridge, bridge (literally bamboo) (nāsā-vaṃśa, nasal bridge; probable)

hindi: सीधा मुख और नासावंश यानी नाक की डण्डी।
english: Straight mouth (face) and nose-bridge (nāsāvaṃśa).
notes: Elliptical: no verb. āsya = mouth, also face; 'mouth' is kept with 'face' beside it. nāsāvaṃśa = nasal bridge (probable).

hindi: दोनों हनु यानी जबड़े उभरे हुए नहीं, और वेष यानी पहनावा भी।
english: The two jaws (hanu) not prominent, and the dress (veṣa) too.
notes: Elliptical: no verb. anulbaṇe is dual and agrees with hanū (hanu is feminine); whether 'not prominent' also applies to veṣa is not stated, and veṣa could also mean 'appearance'. The English 'too' renders ca.

hindi: तालु चिकना, और जीभ भी।
english: The palate (tālu) smooth, and the tongue too.
notes: Elliptical: no verb. ślakṣṇam is neuter and agrees with tālu; whether it also applies to jihvā is not stated.

words.gram: dvandva in a negated bahuvrīhi; m. nom. du.

hindi: दोनों होंठ बहुत मोटे या दुबले नहीं, और देह का बन्ध भी।
english: The two lips not very stout or lean, and the structure of the body (deha-bandha) too.
notes: Elliptical: no verb. Whether 'neither very stout nor lean' also applies to deha-bandha is not stated. deha-bandha is literally 'binding/structure of the body' (frame, build).

words.gloss: two manyā (the side-neck vessels; probably the carotid vessels, probable)

hindi: धड़कता हुआ हृदय, और दोनों शंख यानी कनपटियाँ तथा दोनों मन्या यानी सम्भवतः गरदन के दोनों ओर की रक्तवाहिनियाँ।
english: The heart (hṛdaya) with throbbing, and the two temples (śaṅkha) and the two manyā (probably the vessels at the sides of the neck, the carotids).
notes: Elliptical: no verb. sa-spanda (neuter) agrees with hṛdaya; whether it also applies to the temples and manyā is not stated. śaṅkha = temple (standard). manyā = the structures at the sides of the neck, usually the vessels there (probable; the carotid identification is a modern guess).

hindi: तालु, पैर और पेट गरम, और निःश्वास भी।
english: Warm palate, feet and belly, and the outbreath (niḥśvāsa) too.
notes: Elliptical: no verb. soṣma (neuter) agrees with the neuter dvandva; whether niḥśvāsa is also called warm is not stated.

hindi: दोनों कान पीछे की ओर झुके हुए और रोमयुक्त।
english: The two ears bent down at the back, and hairy.
notes: Elliptical: no verb. pṛṣṭhataḥ is 'at/from the back'; the exact placement of the bend is not stated.

words.gloss: drooping (first part of pralambinyau, see flag)

hindi: दोनों भौंहें थोड़ी झुकी हुई।
english: The two eyebrows slightly drooping (pralambin).

text_flags.why: possible: a space was printed inside the word pralambinyau (īṣat-pralambinyau); the two printed tokens 'īṣatpralaṃ' and 'binyau' are read together

notes: The word pralambinyau (dual feminine of pralambin, 'hanging down') is split across the printed tokens by a stray space; the whole word is glossed in the two tokens. Elliptical: no verb.

words.gloss: well; joined; joint, junction; half-moon; shape

hindi: अस्पष्ट छपा वलिभ; भली भाँति जुड़े जोड़ों वाला और अर्धचन्द्र के आकार का माथा; छाते जैसा सिर।
english: (Unclear: the printed 'valibham'); a forehead (lalāṭa) with well-joined joints (sandhi) and the shape of a half-moon; the head like an umbrella.

text_flags.why: possible damage: 'valibha' has no sure reading; kept unsplit and marked unclear

notes: 'valibham' is unreadable (it might begin with vali 'wrinkle, fold'); no meaning is given. Which noun the adjective su-śliṣṭa-sandhi-ardhacandrākṛti belongs to is not certain: lalāṭam (forehead) is the nearest neuter, but 'with well-joined sandhi' could also qualify śiraḥ. The 'ātapatra' (umbrella) comparison is placed with the following noun in the translation. GROUPING: the unit is a series of short noun phrases and does not appear to be a full sentence. Elliptical: no verb.

hindi: केश एक मूल वाले नहीं, कोमल।
english: The hairs (keśa) not single-rooted, soft.

text_flags.why: possible: vowel length, mūla (root) for 'mula'; the final -ā is regular visarga-loss before a voiced consonant (naikamūlāḥ + mṛdavaḥ)

notes: naika-mūla is taken literally 'not having a single root' (na + eka); some would read naika as 'many', i.e. many-rooted; the sense of the phrase is not explained by the text. Elliptical: no verb.

words.gloss: vein, vessel (śirā, standard: vein); bone; joint

hindi: शिरा यानी नस, हड्डी और जोड़ दृढ़ और छिपे हुए।
english: Firm, hidden: the veins (śirā), bones and joints.
notes: Elliptical: no verb. The three words are taken as one neuter dvandva that both adjectives qualify. śirā = vein or vessel (standard: vein).

words.gloss: wind (flatus; vāta); urine; dung (purīṣa); private (parts or matters; guhya, probable: genitals)

hindi: प्रकृति से मुक्त वायु, मूत्र, मल और गुह्य; हँसना, रोना, अस्पष्ट छपा आर्द्रनि और चेष्टाएँ।
english: Wind (vāta, flatus), urine, dung (purīṣa) and private parts or matters (guhya), released naturally; laughing, weeping, (unclear: the printed 'ārdrani') and activities.

text_flags.why: possible: 'ārdrani' is not a word; kept as printed and marked unclear in the translation

notes: 'prakṛti-mukta' is taken literally, 'released by (in) the natural way'; whether it governs all the items is not stated. vāta here is wind/flatus (not the humour). guhya = private parts or private matters (probable: genitals). 'hasitaruditārdrani' is doubtful at the end ('ārdra' means 'moist'); only hasita and rudita are firm. The ceṣṭitāni item is translated 'activities'. Elliptical: no verb. Low confidence.

words.gram: ppp. √snā, ppp. anu-√lip; n. nom./acc. sg.

hindi: तथा स्नान किया और लेप लगा, नीचे फैले हुए क्रम से सूखता हुआ शरीर इष्ट है।
english: Likewise, desirable is the body (śarīra), bathed and anointed, drying in the order of the downward spread.
notes: The closing 'iti' ends the long description begun at u118 ('iṣṭaṃ ca punar …'); GROUPING: appears to complete the series of u118–u135 (the text does not state the pairing). The exact sense of 'adhaḥ-prasṛta-ānupūrvyā' is taken as 'in due order, spread downward'; what spreads (water, unguent) is not stated. The closing 'iti' is not translated.

hindi: और इस विषय में है:
english: And on this matter there is:
notes: Formula introducing the verses that follow; the thing that 'is' (a verse) is not stated, so nothing is supplied and the English ends with a colon.

words.gloss: more and more; good; field, body

hindi: उत्तरोत्तर उत्तम क्षेत्र वाला, गर्भ से आरम्भ करके रोगरहित।
english: (One) with a field (kṣetra) better and better, free from disease from the garbha (embryo; or womb) onward.
notes: A continuation of the series of adjectives (no noun stated; GROUPING: the construction appears to continue in u139–u141). 'su-kṣetra' = good field; kṣetra also means 'body', but the text is not explained. garbha can mean embryo or womb; 'from the garbha onward' is kept literal. 'uttarottara' = 'one after another, increasingly'.

hindi: आयाम, ज्ञान और विज्ञान से धीरे धीरे बढ़ता हुआ, शुभ।
english: Auspicious, growing slowly by length (āyāma), knowledge (jñāna) and specialised knowledge (vijñāna).
notes: A continuation of the adjectives of u138. āyāma can mean 'length, extension' or 'restraint' (as in prāṇāyāma); 'length' is kept as the literal sense, but the meaning in this context is open. The doubled dd (varddhamāna) is normalised.

hindi: इस प्रकार सब गुणों से युक्त शरीर में सौ शरद् यानी सौ वर्ष।
english: Thus, in a body endowed with all qualities, a hundred autumns (years).
notes: Elliptical: no verb. 'a hundred autumns' is the usual idiom for a hundred years; the next unit begins with āyuḥ 'life-span', so the two units appear to be read together (GROUPING: appears to continue in u141). śarīreśaradāṃ is printed without a space; e + ś has no sandhi, so the split is regular.

hindi: आयु, ऐश्वर्य और सब इष्ट भाव स्थापित हैं।
english: Life-span (āyus), lordship (aiśvarya) and all desired states (bhāva) are established.
notes: The token is āyuḥ + aiśvaryam + iṣṭāḥ + ca (the last ca is joined in the print: 'iṣṭāśca'); the words are split accordingly. 'iṣṭāḥ' is taken with 'sarve bhāvāḥ'. It appears to continue u140 (a body endowed with all qualities); the text does not state this.

hindi: अहंकार और दीनता के बिना सुख और दुःख को भोगता है।
english: (One) experiences pleasure and pain without arrogance and without dejection.
notes: The subject of sevate is not stated ('one'). anutseka and adainya are taken adverbially (neuter accusative) with the verb. utseka = arrogance, pride; dainya = dejection, wretchedness. It appears to continue u141; the text does not state this.
lines_deva: अनुत्सेकमदैन्यं च सुखं दुःखं च सेवते
lines_iast: anutsekamadainyaṃ ca sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ ca sevate

words.gram: pres. part. mid. √tap, m. nom. sg.

words.gloss: of the nature of rajas, rājasa
of the nature of tamas, tāmasa (conjectural reading)

hindi: सत्त्वान्, परन्तु तप्यमान, राजस, किसी प्रकार भी अनुमानित पाठ पर तामस नहीं।
english: But sattvān, being heated (tapyamāna): rājasa, not at all tāmasa (on a conjectural reading).

text_flags.why: possible: s/t confusion in the print; 'tāmataḥ' is not a word, tāmasa balances rājasa; the printed -ataḥ is not an ablative suffix here

notes: The sense of 'sattvān tapyamānaḥ' is uncertain: sattvān is a regular sandhi form (sattvān + tapyamānaḥ), accusative plural of sattva ('beings' or the quality), but it is not clear what it depends on (tap with an accusative is odd); tapyamāna may mean 'being tormented' or 'practising austerity'. The translation keeps the Sanskrit words and does not resolve them. 'tāmataḥ' is read as tāmasaḥ, hence the conjectural mark. The unit appears to be the second half of a sentence begun in u142 (not stated). Low confidence.

words.gloss: giving; conduct, character (śīla); compassion; truth (conjectural reading); continence (brahmacarya); gratitude

hindi: दान, शील, दया, अनुमानित पाठ पर सत्य, ब्रह्मचर्य और कृतज्ञता।
english: Giving (dāna), conduct (śīla), compassion (dayā), truth (on a conjectural reading), continence (brahmacarya) and gratitude (kṛtajñatā).

text_flags.why: possible: 'dayāstya' lacks the vowel after s (dayā-satya); 'astya' is not a word and 'satya' fits a list of virtues

notes: A list of qualities. Elliptical: no verb; it appears to be the subject of u145 (rasāyanāni …), but the text does not state this. brahmacarya = continence (celibacy); śīla = conduct, character. Reviewer: dayā-asteya (non-stealing) is an alternative to the conjectured dayā-satya for printed 'dayāstya'; not applied.

hindi: रसायन यानी कायाकल्प के साधन, मैत्री, और पुण्य तथा आयु की वृद्धि के कारण वाला गुण।
english: Rasāyanas (rejuvenation measures), friendliness (maitrī), and the quality (guṇa) that is the cause of increase of merit and life-span.

text_flags.why: possible: no space was printed between ca and puṇya (spacing error)

notes: Elliptical: no verb. guṇaḥ is singular as printed (a plural guṇāḥ would suit the list better; not corrected). Whether this unit completes the list of u144 is not stated. rasāyana = rejuvenation measure; the text does not say what is meant here.

hindi: इस प्रकार प्रकृतिभेदीय नामक आठवाँ अध्याय।
english: Thus the eighth chapter, named Prakṛtibhedīya (concerning the divisions of prakṛti).
notes: Colophon of the chapter. prakṛtibhedīya = 'concerning the divisions (bheda) of prakṛti (natural constitution)'.
